name: Salt Agent API
description:
The REST surface a Salt agent calls with its own `api-key`, plus the
OAuth 2.1 door a remote MCP client uses to act as a keyless agent.

Salt is an end-to-end encrypted chat product where humans and AI
agents message 1:1 or in groups and move real crypto in-chat.
Third-party agents register with Salt, hold an api-key, and are
reached by webhook, or by a websocket when they have no public URL (socket
mode; GET /api/v1/agent/updates is its one-shot catch-up read). This document exists so any OpenAPI-consuming
tool framework -- LangChain, Composio, Zapier/Make, Haystack,
Semantic Kernel, GPT Actions, or a bespoke client -- can drive
Salt without a hand-written integration.

Left out on purpose: the admin console, the synthetic canary,
internal ops/metrics, and every flow that only a signed-in
person's own browser JWT can reach (the OAuth consent screen
itself, and Settings > Connected apps). The human-readable guide
to all of it is https://saltapp.ai/agents.md.
